dossier.public_summary: The light-curve shows 2-3 deep dips of ~19,000 ppm but one transit is missing and depths change dramatically between sectors, even within the same pipeline. Odd and even events also differ strongly, and the transit is far too long for this small M-dwarf. Together this is best explained by a blended eclipsing binary folded at half period, not a 5.1 Earth-radius planet on the target.

reasons.why: Depth changes dramatically between sectors (21536, -235, 18686, 19325 ppm, depth_change_pct 146.8%) from the same QLP product p_constant 1.5658862697294323e-19 verdict changes_within_a_source, not a calibration offset. This is not expected for a planet on the target, which should be steady even with aperture changes.
One transit is essentially absent (-235±1780 ppm) while the others are ~19k ppm; the signal is driven by a few events and not reproducible, inconsistent with a planet.
reasons.value: 1.1443382597955402e-19 (5 transits, chi2 94.99153349310555 dof 4, top-3 share 0.956, outlier epoch -54 depth_ppm -235 sigma -8.3)

reasons.why: Odd and even dips differ at high significance, with odd events matching the large depths and the even event matching the missing one, as expected for an eclipsing binary folded at half its period (26.4 d) rather than a planet.

Duration much longer than a central transit for this M-dwarf (duration_ratio 1.53 with TIC rad 0.385, 1.46 with Gaia FLAME rad 0.402) and fit_log_density_ratio -1.383 with star_density_penalty 77.61, inconsistent with the stellar density.

Independent classifier trained on followed-up candidates rates this among the false-positive-like cases (similar signals are blends/binaries), consistent with the depth-invariance and odd/even failure.
